A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoVE/ROVE research. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix F report original regression and stochastic-programming experiments, including costs, tail probabilities, hyperparameter analyses, and running times.

after.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain original empirical results and add decision-tree comparisons and further tail-probability results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same subsampling, model retrieval, voting, and data-splitting procedures. The adaptive optimality-threshold rule is also unchanged. Decision trees are additional evaluated base learners, without changes to the proposed ensemble procedure.

E1.justification: v5 Figure 12 adds a synthetic regression scenario with ten uniform inputs and a weighted sinusoidal response. Existing logarithmic and linear regression scenarios, all six UCI datasets, and the five stochastic-programming problems remain. Three UCI plots move to the appendix.

E2.justification: v5 Figures 3 and 12 introduce evaluated comparisons with Random Forests, Gradient Boosted Decision Trees, and XGBoost. This substantially broadens the comparator set beyond v4's base-learner references and MLP bagging comparison.

E3.justification: v5 adds tree-specific protocols, including matched RF tree counts, boosting early stopping, and dedicated subsample sizes. Also, v4 Appendix F.1 specifies real-data MLP widths of 100, 300, 300, 100; v5 Appendix E.1 removes this exception and lists 50, 300, 300, 50 generally. This changes reported settings without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new tree experiments extend sensitivity analysis of comparative performance across Pareto tail shapes, examining when ROVE/ROVEs outperform conventional ensembles. Existing subsample-size, ensemble-size, threshold, optimum-multiplicity, and correlation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 200 independently generated synthetic datasets, 100 real-data permutations, and 95% confidence intervals for average costs. No changed seed disclosure, repeated-run practice, or statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v5 adds bagging tail curves in Figure 2d–f and substantial comparative tree results in Figures 3 and 12. These show advantages for ROVE/ROVEs in extreme tails under heavier noise, while conventional ensembles can perform better under lighter noise. Every original result plot is retained unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1 and its formal counterpart C.7/B.7 replace total bad-output probability with the maximum probability of an individual bad model, refining the stated condition and proof. This gap already appeared in v4's general Theorem C.8, limiting the theoretical novelty. Example 1.1 also adds the necessary restriction that delta lies between zero and one.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify the broad base-learner-agnostic enhancement claim by requiring reasonable predictive performance and satisfaction of the theorem conditions. The central contributions—model-level voting and polynomial-to-exponential tail enhancement—remain.

C2.justification: Sections 2.1 and 5 extend the earlier shallow-network bias observation into a general subsampling bias–tail tradeoff and applicability limitation. Appendix E.4 newly suggests that limited benefits on three real datasets may reflect lighter tails.

D1.justification: v5 newly reports personal-computer execution and a Gurobi requirement, and supplies tree-training controls and the sinusoidal data-generation formula. It removes the separate real-data MLP architecture specification. The existing code link is retained and relocated.

R1.justification: v5 adds Chen and Guestrin (2016), Geurts et al. (2006), and Kwon et al. (2021), extending the tree-ensemble and median-of-means references. Most related-work discussion is retained; the additional review formerly in Appendix A moves into Section 4.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the abstract, methodological explanation, and experimental narrative. Additional related work moves into the main text, Section 5 becomes Conclusion and Limitations, and appendices are reorganized. Most prose and the core section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with redesigned author/title formatting, removed running headers, and rescaled figures. Figure 2 expands from three to six panels, the real-data figure is split between main text and appendix, and new tree figures are added.

improvement.justification: The new comparative tail results better support the paper's central empirical argument, while qualified claims and explicit bias limitations improve its accuracy and usefulness. The theoretical refinement is limited because the underlying gap-based result already existed. Removing the real-data architecture exception creates reproducibility ambiguity alongside unchanged plots, but this limited drawback does not outweigh the clearer scope and stronger comparative evidence.
